{{Short description|Measure derived from a random measure}}
In [[probability theory]], an '''intensity measure''' is a [[measure (mathematics)|measure]] that is derived from a [[random measure]]. The intensity measure is a non-random measure and is defined as the [[expectation value]] of the random measure of a set, hence it corresponds to the average volume the random measure assigns to a set. The intensity measure contains important information about the properties of the random measure. A [[Poisson point process]], interpreted as a random measure, is for example uniquely determined by its intensity measure.<ref name="Klenke528" />

== Definition ==
Let <math> \zeta </math> be a [[random measure]] on the [[measurable space]] <math> (S, \mathcal A) </math> and denote the [[expected value]] of a random element <math> Y </math> with <math> \operatorname E [Y] </math>.

The intensity measure 
:<math> \operatorname E \zeta \colon \mathcal A \to [0,\infty] </math>
of <math> \zeta </math> is defined as
:<math>  \operatorname E \zeta(A)= \operatorname E[\zeta(A)] </math>
for all <math> A \in \mathcal A</math>.<ref name="Klenke526" /><ref name="Kallenberg53" />

Note the difference in notation between the expectation value of a random element <math> Y </math>, denoted by <math> \operatorname E [Y] </math> and the intensity measure of the random measure <math> \zeta </math>, denoted by <math> \operatorname E\zeta </math>.

== Properties ==
The intensity measure <math> \operatorname E\zeta </math> is always  [[s-finite measure|s-finite]] and satisfies
:<math>\operatorname E \left[ \int f(x) \; \zeta(\mathrm dx)\right]=  \int f(x) \operatorname E\zeta(dx)</math>

for every positive [[measurable function]] <math> f </math> on <math> (S, \mathcal A) </math>.<ref name="Kallenberg53" />
